replace_en.old: वृषस्व (*vṛṣasva*)—जठरे सिंच । यथा नाभेरधो न पतति तथा धारयेति भावः । (*jaṭhare siṃca | yathā nābheradho na patati tathā dhārayeti bhāvaḥ |*) In this verse it is plainly said पिब (*piba*), "drink the Soma juice"; is not the use of the word वृषस्व (*vṛṣasva*) then useless? The answer: since Indra is famous as extremely fond of drinking Soma juice, the use of the two words पिब (*piba*) and वृषभ (*vṛṣabha*) ⟨NOTE:12⟩ is also proper, to stress plainly: "when drinking Soma, drink as much as you wish, so that it does not fall below the navel, and drink so that the inner part of the belly is well soaked and refreshed."

replace_en.old: As the words of the Supreme Person say, उत्तीदेयुरिमे लोकाः न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहं (*uttīdeyurime lokāḥ na kuryāṃ karma cedahaṃ*)⟨NOTE:29⟩—"if I did not perform action, all the worlds would perish"—so, if Indra, the lord of the universe, were not constantly engaged in action useful for the conduct of the world, the ruin of the world would be certain. He is the cause of the appearance of Dawn and of the rising of the sun. As described in स्वराजः, महतः, ते (*svarājaḥ, mahataḥ, te*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-46-1), he alone is lord of the whole universe and holds sovereign rank. Even so, because the performance of sacrifice nourishes the world and is the cause of the growth of prosperity of the whole world, of gods, men and others, it is said that Indra honoured Dawn and the Sun, the primary causes of that sacrifice. The purport of the present Ṛk is that, though himself the lord, he worshipped his own creation, which nourishes the world.

replace_en.old: The word kuvāri⟨NOTE:44⟩ in general means a man who is extremely selfish, miserly, performs no sacrifice and leads a contemptible life. In the present ṛk, where akavārim stands, the word kava means a small, despised person, and the compound is kava-ari: a petty enemy. One who is not a kavāri is an akavāri, that is, an enemy of great power; or an abundant number may also be indicated by it. It is an epithet showing Indra's greatness: one who can face such enemies.

replace_en.old: The sūkta beginning चर्षणीधृतं (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ*) has twelve Ṛks and is Vaiśvāmitra (its seer is Viśvāmitra) and Aindra (its deity is Indra). The Anukramaṇikā says: चर्षणीधृतं द्वादशाद्यांत्यौ तृचौ जागतगायत्राविति (*carṣaṇīdhṛtaṃ dvādaśādyāṃtyau tṛcau jāgatagāyatrāviti*), i.e. the first triplet is in Jagatī, the last triplet in Gāyatrī, and the remaining Ṛks are in Triṣṭubh. The use of the sūkta is Laiṅgika (by the indication of the text). In the ukthya rite (the Kannada reading उक्ते क्रत्वा (*ukte kratvā*) is garbled) ⟨NOTE:60⟩, in the Maitrāvaruṇa śastra, after the anurūpa triplet, the first triplet of this sūkta is to be recited. It is stated in the sūtra: चर्षणीधृतमस्तभ्नाद्दामसुर इति तृचौ (*carṣaṇīdhṛtamastabhnāddāmasura iti tṛcau*) (Ā. 6-1). At the Viṣuvat in the niṣkevalya the triplet नृणामु त्वा (*nṛṇāmu tvā*) is used; this is stated in the Viṣuvān section: नृणामु त्वा नृतमं गीर्भिरुक्थैरिति शिस्त्रः (*nṛṇāmu tvā nṛtamaṃ gīrbhirukthairiti śistraḥ*) ⟨NOTE:61⟩ (Ā. 8-6). In the Bṛhaspatisava also this triplet is used as the nivid in the niṣkevalya; the sūtra says: नृणामु त्वैति मध्यंदिनः (*nṛṇāmu tvaiti madhyaṃdinaḥ*) (Ā. 9-5). In the Mahāvrata also this triplet is used in the niṣkevalya.

replace_en.old: Of the god Agni, सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*) — of good wealth, one who is to be well resorted to — the संदृक् (*saṃdṛk*) (sight, glance) is श्रेष्ठा (*śreṣṭhā*), exceedingly praiseworthy; among mortals it is चित्रतमा (*citratamā*), most to be honoured and worshipped, and it is स्पार्हा (*spārhā*), to be desired by all. An illustration follows. As, for a man who desires milk, the शुचि (*śuci*) (bright, full of splendour) घृतं (*ghṛtaṃ*), the heated (सप्तं (*saptaṃ*)) milk of the अघ्न्या (*aghnyā*) cow that flows forth, is desirable; ⟨NOTE:345⟩ so too the sight is desired. There is a second illustration: as, for a mortal begging for a cow, the मंहना (*maṃhanā*) of a milch cow — मंहति (*maṃhati*) is a root meaning giving — ⟨NOTE:346⟩ that is, as a gift is pleasing, so is it. The rest gives accent and derivation of सुभगस्य (*subhagasya*), स्मार्हा (*smārhā*) and देवस्य (*devasya*) (Grammar section).
